key_insight: Randomly projecting each quantum state copy into a smaller subspace lets multi-copy nonlinear measurements be done with far less coherent hardware, at the cost of more repeated state preparations.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum hardware teams a tunable way to match protocol complexity to device limits by trading expensive collective operations for additional sampling.
method: Apply Haar-random projection from an n-qubit space to a q-qubit subspace before the collective measurement.
Perform the multi-copy measurement only on the reduced Hilbert space.
Use derived averaging formulas to convert projected moments back to multivariate traces and estimate the copy overhead.
evidence_signal: The abstract provides an analytic scaling law: estimating tr(ρ^K) after compressing from n to q qubits needs about O(2^((n-q)(K-1))) copies, i.e., each removed qubit multiplies sampling cost by 2^(K-1).
watch_item: The reduced coherent resource demand comes with rapidly growing sampling overhead, so the method may become costly for large compression ratios or large K.
paper_title: Random Projections for Multi-Copy Quantum Algorithms
